skillRoll.description: Year Zero Engine's core dice-pool mechanic (standard d6-pool variant, not the optional step-dice variant used by games like Twilight 2000): roll a pool of Base Dice (equal to the attribute score) plus Skill Dice (equal to the skill level), all d6, and count each die showing a 6 as one success; at least one success is required to succeed. Confirmed against crates/thunderforge-dice's real grammar: `attribute` and `skill` are placeholder-bound scores summed inside the parenthesized dice-count expression (a real grammar feature, per the existing `(skill)d6kh3x=6cs>=4` formula in that crate's own test suite), producing a single d6 pool so `cs>=6` counts successes across the combined pool in one pass. Two separately-counted pools added with `+` (e.g. `{attribute}d6cs>=6+{skill}d6cs>=6`) also parses, but the dice engine only classifies a formula's ResolutionKind as SuccessCount when success-counting happens on a single top-level dice/pool node, so the two-pool-added-together form would evaluate to the correct numeric total but be reported as a Total, not a SuccessCount — the single-combined-pool form above is the correct one for this mechanic. Gear Dice are a further additive pool this pass intentionally leaves out of the formula (out of scope per this pass's plan).

placeholders.attribute: The chosen attribute's score (1-5): strength, agility, wits, or empathy.
